profile.headline: Software Engineer IV at MPL Corporation
profile.summary:
High-tech (R&D) experience in the communications and information services sectors, especially in the support of broadband and wireless telecom, and artificial intelligence and DoD related developments, including DARPA funded R&D.

Technology business planning & systems development: from CONOPS development, to trade study, process re-engineering, system prototyping and demonstration, development, and commercial rollout of new technologies in support of new business endeavors.

Professional speaker & consultant: to various professional groups and conferences. Authored chapters in two university books ('04 and '05). 

GOAL:
My background encompasses both telecom and information technologies.  A position that could benefit from such a broad background would be attractive.  Service oriented architectures (e.g., SOA, the DOD GIG); advanced telecom systems (e.g., IMS, NG-911), advanced distributed system networks (e.g., 3G, 4G, LTE); and advanced systems (Big Data, Clouds, simulators).  An attractive opportunity would allow me to continue to expand my technical knowledge and to apply it in delivering new solutions, or enhancing existing products and services for my employer.

BACKGROUND
POSITIONS:   Scientist, Numerical Analyst, Systems Engineer, Software Engineer, Telecom Engineer, Technology Business Planner, Enterprise Architect, Project Manager
TELECOM:    Internet, AIN, VoIP, SIP, IMS, WebRTC, 4G, LTE, WiMax, M2M, SensorNet, NG-911
IT:    SOA, DoDAF, FEA, OOAD, SDLC, geographic information systems (GIS), real-time, embedded systems, high-fidelity simulators, man-machine systems, V&V
SCIENCE:    Numerical analysis, signal processing, simulators, artificial intelligence, knowledge systems, machine learning, pattern analysis, neural networks, human factors analysis
LANGUAGES & TOOLS:   C/C++, Java (SE ME EE), Fortran, Lisp, ADA, UML, SysML, SQL, Eclipse, Rational, Rhapsody, KloxWork, ARINC, Object Oriented Databases, MS Office

positions.title: Software Engineer IV
positions.description:
Support MPL contract with NASA IV&V in Fairmont, WV.
Perform independent validation and verification (IV&V) of various NASA systems. This activity spans from requirements and design validation, through implementation validation, static code analysis, unit and build testing, and system rollout.

positions.title: Metrics Analyst
positions.description: In support of a NASA contract, provides advice, guidance, and recommendations regarding the application of software and system metrics that allow measurement of the effectiveness and efficiency of the program and the achievement of program goals and outcomes. Performs detailed analyses on NASA project and program data to generate metrics gauging project status and performance. Establishes and maintains a Goal, Question, Metric (GQM) measurement framework. Develops and maintains NASA IV&V Program Metrics Plan (PMP).

positions.title: Project Manager II
positions.description: Providing project management and technical support to a major enterprise telecom endeavor (a government agency with multiple locations) – upgrading from traditional PSTN-based telecom infrastructure (PBX, Call Center, ACD, IVR, etc.) to a SIP, IMS, VoIP-based infrastructure: IP-PBX with SIP trunking, etc. as well as the introduction of unified communications services and network convergence that such an infrastructure change enables.

positions.title: Principal
positions.description:
Developing and maintaining websites and database applications for The Church of God.  This includes general website design, database design, implementation, and support & maintenance.

Developed Red Cell CONOPS, in collaboration with Telcordia Advanced R&D Labs and ISR, for a nationwide alerting system that would leverage existing and near-term technologies (e.g., national cellular infrastructure) the Next Generation 911 (NG-911) and the Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN) to provide: detection and modeling of threats; national and regional situation awareness and coordination; efficient planning and execution of alert notifications; continuous response processing; and status updating.

positions.title: Sr. Scientist
positions.description:
Performed NASA IVV CD (Capability Development) project examining emerging technologies employed by NASA, including Model-Based Software Engineering (MBSE) and ARINC, employed by Orion/MPCV (Multi-Person Crew Vehicle) project.

Performed NASA IV&V in the independent validation and verification of NASA systems, specifically for JUNO—mission to Jupiter.  This activity spans from requirements and design validation, to static code analysis and unit and build testing.

Provided technical guidance for major wireless (WiMAX) effort targeted at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) first-responder community. Contributing to new business development in the areas of communications targeted at the DOD GIG world, as well as the Internet world (SIP, IMS, VoIP).

positions.title: Prinicipal Member R&D Staff
positions.description:
Developed strategy, DoDAF compliant architecture, and phased development plan for a DoD/IC customer for the introduction of machine-to-machine (M2M) services, aligned with the DoD net-centric service oriented paradigm, and implemented within DoD’s Global Information Grid (GIG).

Developed 5-year technology forecast/trade study for major defense contractor regarding evolution of man-machine interface and collaboration, and the technologies to support those changes.

Developed CONOPS, business case, trade study, technology assessment, network architecture, & deployment strategy for major government customer for high-throughput (multi-terabit per day) real-time distributed data acquisition and processing systems. (Two years later, this effort served as the basis for the agency’s RFP).

Developed neural network-based strategies and methods for the verification and validation of OLNN’s—online learning neural networks.  Paper presented at ASC 2003, and in book chapter 2005.

positions.title: Sr. Member Technical Staff
positions.description:
Connected Family
This development effort was a direct consequence of the successful visibility and internal marketing of the Telecom'95 demonstration convergence concepts (see below). 

Represented GTE/VZ as technical representative to the Open Services Gateway Initiative (OSGi). The OSGi framework standard lead to the mobile Java service platform that is referenced by JSR 232.

positions.title: Mgr. Technology Business Planning
positions.description:
Provided direction and oversight to Telops-related R&D programs at GTE Labs.  Coordinated with major equipment and service providers (e.g., standards body memberships) in the development of emerging communications technologies.  Developed technology appraisals and policy/program guidance for the development, procurement, and roll-out of these technologies and services.

Example strategic decisions that Mr Smith championed at GTE. Developed the justification (trade study) for adoption of the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) as the core VoIP control protocol. Developed the justification for adopting IP switching (introduced by the start-up Ipsilon, and now the heart of MPLS technology) in preference to further expansion of Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) technology.

positions.title: Mgr. Process Re-engineering
positions.description:
GTE High Value Capabilities Definition & Assessment:
Transferred to GTE Telops.  Developed new CONOPS, systems architecture, etc. as part of major “Process Re-engineering” effort, the precursor to today’s SOA—Service Oriented Architecture, and UML-enabled model-based systems engineering (MBSE). Responsible for the Advanced Services component of the process re-engineering effort, which leveraged prior work in the AIN Testbed. Showcased results of this effort in a demonstration developed for Telecom’95 (see below).

AIN Development:
Developed conceptual design of, and provided technical direction for GTE contracted development of GTE’s own commercial AIN Service Creation and Service Logic Execution Environments—SCE and SLEE.

Telecom'95 Demonstration:
Led development of a service concept demonstration of converged services—a world in which wireline services, cell phones, and networked home appliances (TV, radio, etc.) cooperate to deliver user customizable converged services.

positions.title: Sr. Member Technical Staff
positions.description:
AIN Systems & Services Development:
As a member of GTE Labs, worked with GTE Telops (in Irving, TX) supporting GTE's AIN (Advanced Intelligent Networks) development effort.  Setup and operated an R&D test-bed that included a captive Class 5 switch, SS7 service, SCPs SSPs, various service creation/deployment environments. Co-developed AIN systems and services with vendors, e.g., of Telcordia (nee Bellcore) and Lucent (nee AT&T Labs) supporting testing of their in-development platforms.

positions.title: Sr. Member R&D Staff
positions.description:
Expert System Toolset Development:
Developed a C-based expert system toolset supporting the blackboard paradigm of distributed, cooperative knowledge sources—a branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The toolset, similar to the prior porting to ADA, was targeted at real-time applications, e.g., TDRSS satellite monitoring and control.

positions.title: Member Technical Staff
positions.description:
GIS—Geographical Reasoning System
Developed intelligent geographical reasoning system (GIS) for the Lisp machine environment.  Oversaw porting of system to a traditional (C-based) computing environment for use in contractual government programs.

Expert System Shell Development
Developed editor/inspector/debugger environment to support the development of applications that utilize the blackboard (distributed) expert system paradigm.  Later, ported this environment to ADA.

positions.title: Scientist Associate
positions.description:
DARPA Pilot’s Associate
Developed the system architecture and implementation approach for embedding artificial intelligence (expert system) technology—including distributed intelligence, data fusion methods, etc—within the airborne cockpit environment.  This IR&D effort laid the foundation for Lockheed winning a major ($6M) DARPA contract.

positions.title: Research Scientist II
positions.description:
Radar Algorithm Development
Developed and validated effectiveness of new radar signal processing algorithms for implementation in real-time target discrimination and classification systems.  Developed new algorithms leading to DARPA contracts to demonstrate new algorithms.

Real-time System S/W Development
Developed systems for simulation and real-time testing of radar systems. Directed the development of software libraries implementing signal processing.
